feature: grouped options for select and multiple select filters (#5012)

Select fields can split a long list into labeled groups with
`grouped_options`, but the select and multiple select filters could only
list their options flat. A filter over many values (cities, departments,
skills) had no way to show which group each one belongs to.

A filter's `options` map each option id to its label. A Hash in place of
a label is now a group: its key labels an <optgroup> and the Hash holds
that group's own id => label options, so the filter keeps the shape it
already uses for its options:

    def options
      {
        "Europe" => {fr: "France", de: "Germany"},
        "Asia" => {jp: "Japan"}
      }
    end

Ungrouped options can sit next to groups and keep their place. `apply`
still receives the option ids, and the applied value is selected inside
its group. Filters without a Hash in their options render exactly as
before.

The multiple select box sizes itself from the rows it lists, so it counts
each group label as a row next to the options.

The Volunteer resource in the dummy app gets a department and a skills
filter that group their options like its grouped select fields do, and
the toolbar spec that relied on Volunteer having no filters now uses
Store.

feature: actions started from an association panel know the panel's parent (#5011)

* feature: actions started from an association panel know the panel's parent

An action run from a has_many or has_and_belongs_to_many panel had no way
to reach the record holding the panel. The visible block got
parent_resource while the dropdown rendered, but fields, handle and the
modal blocks did not, so actions like "clone this template into the
group" had to smuggle the parent id through encoded arguments.

Actions now take parent_record and parent_resource, and expose both to
fields, handle and every block they evaluate (name, visible, authorize,
confirmation, the modal texts and button options). Both are nil when the
action wasn't started from an association.

How the parent travels:

- BaseController#set_actions and ResourceComponent#row_actions hand the
  panel's parent to the actions they build.
- BaseAction#link_arguments (now an instance method that wraps the class
  one) adds via_resource_class and via_record_id to the action link,
  next to the via_related_name the panel already sends. Custom control
  actions get the parent hydrated in RendersControls#render_action and
  their link gets the same params.
- The modal form and navigate_to_action keep all three params, so the
  run and the next action in a multi-step flow see the same parent.

Those are request params, so ActionsController#set_parent looks the
parent up the way the panel did and asks what the panel asked before
handing it over:

- the parent resource must exist and the named field must be one of its
  panel fields (has_one, has_many, has_and_belongs_to_many, array) that
  lists the action's resource, or the request is a 404;
- the parent's view_<association>? and act_on_<association>? policy
  methods must allow it, or the request is refused, the same checks
  that show the panel and its Actions button.

The lookup and the view check are extracted from
build_association_scope_from_params into set_parent_from_via_params, so
the summary chart and the actions controller share them. An unknown
via_resource_class is now a 404 there too instead of a NoMethodError.

ArrayField#target_resource returns the resource the panel lists. The
inherited one reflected on an Active Record association that array
fields don't have, so the association check crashed for them.

The dummy app gets a Test::ShowParent action on reviews. Request specs
cover the panel links, the modal blocks and fields, the form, handle,
navigate_to_action, an array panel, actions without a parent, and the
refusals for a wrong association, a non-panel field, an unknown parent
resource and denied view_/act_on_ policies.

Fixes https://github.com/avo-hq/avo/issues/3165

* docs(skills): actions read the association panel's parent

The avo-actions skill said the parent reached only visible, as parent_resource.record, and that a run checked only
the children's act_on?. Also trims two code comments to two lines.

feature: key option to choose where file and files fields store uploads (#5009)

* feature: key option to choose where file and files fields store uploads

Active Storage stores every upload under a random blob key, so the files
in a bucket can't be matched back to their records by name. Its `attach`
takes a `key:` for that, and the `file` and `files` fields now forward
one:

    field :photos, as: :files,
      key: -> { "photos/#{record.to_param}/#{file.original_filename}" }

The option takes a string or a block. The block runs through
ExecutionContext with the record, the resource, the field and the
uploaded file, so a `files` field can give each file its own key. A
block that returns nothing keeps Active Storage's random key. Blob keys
are unique, so a key that's already taken fails the save with the
database's error, like it does for `attach`.

Only files uploaded through the form get the key. A direct upload or a
Media Library pick arrives as the signed id of a blob that's already in
storage, and goes through unchanged. On the `file` field the key is
applied after `update_using`, which still gets the uploaded file.

Fixes https://github.com/avo-hq/avo/issues/2890

* Show a taken storage key on the field instead of the database error

Blob keys are unique and a replaced file's blob is purged after the new one
is saved, so re-uploading a file under the same key failed the save with a raw
PG::UniqueViolation. The field now adds "has already been taken" during the
fill, which save_record stops on, and refuses two files of one upload that
compute the same key. Also teaches the avo-fields skill the key option.

feature: app-wide default display formats for date, date_time and time fields (#5006)

* feature: app-wide default display formats for date, date_time and time fields

Date, DateTime and Time fields each take a `format:` option (Luxon tokens)
for how they display on index and show pages. An app that wants the same
format everywhere had to repeat it on every field, including the
created_at/updated_at timestamps most resources show.

Add three configuration options that set the format those fields fall
back to when they don't pass their own:

    Avo.configure do |config|
      config.date_format = "dd.LL.yyyy"
      config.date_time_format = "dd.LL.yyyy HH:mm"
      config.time_format = "HH:mm"
    end

They default to the formats the fields already used ("yyyy-LL-dd",
"yyyy-LL-dd TT" and "TT"), so nothing changes for apps that don't set
them. A field's own `format:` still wins. Each field type reads its own
option, so TimeField (a DateTimeField subclass) doesn't pick up the
date_time format. The flatpickr `picker_format` used on forms stays a
per-field option, since it takes a different token set.

The generated initializer lists the three options next to timezone and
currency.

Specs cover the defaults, the configured value, the field option winning
over it, and the formats the show and index pages hand to the date-field
controller.

* Teach the shipped skills the app-wide date and time formats

avo-admin-config lists config.date_format, date_time_format and time_format;
avo-fields points the date/time format: option at them.

fix: ignore encoded_filters values that don't decode to filters (#4989)

BaseFilter.decode_filters parsed the param without any handling, so a
truncated URL raised JSON::ParserError and the index answered with a 500.
JSON that isn't an object and a repeated param failed as well.

With session persistence the failure outlived the request. The value is
saved to the session before it's decoded, so every later visit to that
index read it back and failed too, until the session was cleared.

Decode anything that isn't a filters hash to an empty hash, so the page
renders without those filters, the way stale filter classes are already
discarded.

fix: distribution chart adds up the counts of values sharing a label (#4988)

* fix: distribution chart adds up the counts of values sharing a label

compute_summary_data built its labels with `transform_keys`, which keeps
only one value when two keys map to the same label. NULL and "" both show
as the blank label, and two associated records can have the same title,
so one group's count silently replaced the other's. The popover showed a
wrong number and the full page chart computed its percentages from a
total missing those records.

Add the counts of colliding labels together, then sort again because the
merged count can belong higher than where the query's order put it. The
`reorder` stays, since it also clears the index query's default order,
which would be invalid next to GROUP BY.

* fix: equal counts keep the query's order in the distribution chart

sort_by isn't stable, so labels with the same count could swap places between page loads.

Co-authored-by: Paul Bob <paul.ionut.bob@gmail.com>

fix: Media Library delete removes the file and refuses attached blobs (#4987)

MediaLibraryController#destroy called `@blob.destroy!`. Active Storage's
`destroy` only removes the database row, so deleting an unattached file
left it in the storage service with nothing pointing at it, and on a blob
still in use it raised ActiveRecord::InvalidForeignKey, which reached the
user as an error page.

Use `purge`, which also deletes the file, and check for attachments first
so an attached blob is refused with a message on its edit page, the same
way a blank filename is refused on update.

Both redirects are now 303s. A `fetch` keeps DELETE across a 302, and
neither target has a DELETE route.
